sections.h2: Where does a Scott County, Kentucky tax bill come from?
sections.html:
The PVA decides what each Scott County parcel is worth, and the sheriff mails and collects the bill. The sheriff's page says the office never sets a value and gathers money for 28 taxing districts in the county, which can include the state, the county, school districts, fire and library districts and sometimes cities that contract for the service. Bills normally go out on November 1. For a value you dispute, call the PVA at (502) 863-7885. For payment questions, call the sheriff at (502) 863-7855.

Georgetown adds a layer of its own. The city runs a separate city property tax, and its Clerk's Office takes payment in person, by mail or by phone, while online payment and bill search run through the city's OpenGov portal. Bills from before 2025 are found through the city's Tax Master service. A house inside Georgetown carries a city bill in addition to the county one.

sections.h2: What does Scott County look like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Scott County sits north of Lexington in the Bluegrass and belongs to the Lexington-Fayette metro area. The General Assembly cut it from Woodford County in 1792 and named it for Gen. Charles Scott. It covers 285 square miles, of which about 3.7 are water, and it borders seven counties: Grant, Harrison, Bourbon, Fayette, Woodford, Franklin and Owen. Georgetown is the seat and the largest city. Sadieville and Stamping Ground are the other two incorporated cities.

The county grew quickly: 33,061 residents in 2000, 47,173 in 2010 and 57,155 in 2020. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 62,262, an increase of 8.9 percent since 2020.

  • Georgetown began as Lebanon, a settlement led to the Royal Spring in 1782, and was renamed for George Washington in 1790.
  • Elijah Craig, who led that settlement, is credited with early mills and possibly the area's first bourbon.
  • The Choctaw Nation operated the Choctaw Academy at Blue Spring in the county from 1825 until 1842.
  • Voters approved countywide alcohol sales in 2019.

Interstate 75 runs along the east side of Georgetown, with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, and Lexington is about 16 miles south. US 25, 62 and 460 also serve the city. Georgetown College sits downtown.

sections.h2: How big is the Toyota effect on Scott County homes?
sections.html:
Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky opened in Georgetown in 1988, its first wholly owned plant in the United States, and it builds the Camry, Lexus ES and RAV4. The city's 2018 annual financial report listed it as the top employer with 10,019 workers, well ahead of Scott County Schools at 1,219. The Census Bureau counts 26,711 jobs at county employers in 2023.

Schools shape demand too. Scott County Schools runs nine elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, and Great Crossing High School opened in 2019 as population climbed. Know which school zone your house falls in before you list it, because relocating families ask.

sections.h2: How do Scott County housing numbers look next to the rest of Kentucky?
sections.html:
Scott is a higher-priced county than most. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a middle owner-occupied value of $288,500 and a middle household income of $85,158. Permits for 393 new buildings were issued in 2025, so a resale competes with builders.

  • Households: 22,642, with an estimated 25,010 housing units by July 1, 2025.
  • Owners occupy 71.7 percent of homes, and median gross rent runs $1,247.
  • Owner costs with a mortgage run $1,637 a month, against $514 without one.
  • The mean commute is 22.2 minutes, and 34.7 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or more.
  • Poverty touches 8.8 percent of residents.

The 2020 census found a median age of 36.2 and about two in three residents living in urban areas. Only 6.2 percent of housing units stood vacant then.

sections.h2: What older neighborhoods and landmarks matter in Georgetown?
sections.html:
Georgetown became a railroad hub after the Civil War, tied to Cincinnati, Louisville and Frankfort lines, and Confederate raiders under John Hunt Morgan struck the town on July 15, 1862 and July 10, 1864. Its downtown business section is the Oxford Historic District, which is on the National Register of Historic Places. Ward Hall, a Greek Revival mansion just outside town, is listed there too.

If your house falls in or near a historic district, ask the city before you plan exterior changes for a sale. Georgetown's humid subtropical climate delivers about 45 inches of rain a year, with the wettest months in late spring and summer, so roof and drainage condition draw the closest looks from buyers.

sections.h2: When is Scott County property tax due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 supplies the dates. Pay everything by November 1 for a 2 percent discount. Between November 2 and December 31 you owe the printed amount. January adds 5 percent, and anything paid after January 31 carries 10 percent.

The tax is a personal debt of whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and a delinquent bill leaves a lien that follows the land. Put the split of this year's bill in your sales contract so the closing agent knows what to pay from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What happens to Scott County bills that go delinquent?
sections.html:
Around April 15 the sheriff's unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. A county attorney's notice in May offers a payment agreement to those who qualify, and a second notice follows in June. The clerk's site spells out each step before the annual sale.

Scott County Clerk delinquent tax calendar
DateStep
April 15Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk
May and JuneCounty Attorney mails notices and offers payment agreements
June 30Deadline to sign a payment agreement
July 1Advertising costs attach to remaining bills
August 21, 4:30 pmLast chance to pay and stay out of the sale
August 24, 8:30 amSale in the third-floor Fiscal Court Room

Those are the dates the clerk published for the 2026 sale, which has already taken place. Expect the same sequence each year with shifted dates. The clerk accepts cash, cashier's checks, money orders and cards, and card payments carry a 2.75 percent vendor fee. For payoff figures call the clerk at (502) 863-7875, extension 2260, or the County Attorney at (502) 863-7870 about agreements.

sections.h2: Where are the Scott County tax offices?
sections.html:
• Sheriff (current-year bills): 240 Caleb Conley Way and 120 N Hamilton St, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Clerk (delinquent bills, deeds, motor vehicles): 101 E Main Street, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Attorney: 198 E Washington St, Georgetown.
  • Georgetown-Scott County Revenue Commission (occupational and business tax): (502) 603-5860.

The county Treasurer's page states that vehicle and property taxes are not collected in that office.

sections.h2: Can I appeal my Scott County valuation, and who gets a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA. Kentucky law requires it before you can file with the board of assessment appeals, and the board expects comparable sales, repair estimates or similar facts. Appealing does not delay the tax, so pay on your own claimed value in the meantime.

Owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled can apply at the PVA for the homestead exemption. The state deduction was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, so a $320,000 assessment would be taxed as $270,900. Ask the PVA what applies to the current year.

faqs.q: Who collects Scott County property tax?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff's Office collects current-year bills, at (502) 863-7855. The County Clerk takes over unpaid bills around April 15, and the Georgetown city clerk handles city property tax separately.

faqs.q: Does Scott County hold its tax sale every year?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's calendar sets the sale for late August. For 2026 it was August 24 at 8:30 am, with payment due by 4:30 pm on August 21 to be removed from it.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan on delinquent Scott County tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. The County Attorney mails a notice in May with payment-agreement options for eligible owners, and the deadline to enter one is June 30. Call (502) 863-7870.

faqs.q: Is a Scott County homeowner who is 65 entitled to the exemption automatically?
faqs.a: No. You apply at the PVA at (502) 863-7885 with proof of age. The state deduction for 2025 and 2026 was $49,100.

faqs.q: Do Georgetown homeowners pay a separate city tax?
faqs.a: Yes, Georgetown bills its own city property tax. The city offers online lookup and payment through OpenGov, and you can also pay at the City Clerk's Office.
